$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

architect.rationale: Single-loop. Goal items 1-3 all edit orchestra/protocol/codec.ts and protocol/fixtures/index.ts, so they cannot be separate slices without overlap; they are one slice, s1. The only disjoint file is core/tests/wire_fixtures.rs, s2: two slices, under the diamond bar. Run s1 then s2 in one worktree, one branch off main 9d8f98f; orchestra is a git repo. Risk s1 HIGH: it changes a compatibility rule, the G6 tolerance extended to transcript entry kinds, in the file three consumers share (desktop vitest, mobile jest, Rust fixtures), and one of its checks can pass vacuously: the Vite JSON import may turn a __proto__ key into an object-literal prototype and drop it from both the wire text and the expected value in desktop, so a green fixture proves nothing there. The reviewer must run the named mutations. No sensitive data. Risk s2 LOW: one test-only Rust file, no sensitive data, no file shared with s1; a green run plus its four mutations failing is sufficient evidence. Item 3, utf8Length: count a lone surrogate, a high not followed by a low or a stray low, as 3 bytes. That equals TextEncoder, which writes U+FFFD at 3 bytes, and WTF-8 at 3 bytes per surrogate, so TextEncoder stays the test oracle. Exact host parity is not a count at all: serde_json rejects a lone surrogate escape at parse, so the host gives bad_request at any length (prior run reviews.s2, codec.rs:222). Rejecting lone surrogates in every TS string is a wider change than the approved undercount fix, and TS-accepts/Rust-rejects is the safe direction on host input, so it is the gate alternative, not the plan. Item 3, __proto__: the key SURVIVES, matching core/src/wire/args.rs:68 BTreeMap<String,String>. Use Object.defineProperty with enumerable, writable and configurable on the plain out object, not Object.create(null), so the decoded value keeps a normal prototype; no class and nothing Babel compiles to a helper. Item 1 is decode-only in TS. desktop/src/types.ts and SessionDetail.tsx are not touched: desktop reads transcripts over Tauri IPC through its own decodeTranscriptRecord in desktop/src/ipc.ts from a host built from the same commit, so it never sees a kind it does not know. Widening only the wire union keeps the Assignable<desktop, wire> lock in protocol.test.ts:43-50 valid, since desktop stays a subset. The Rust Entry enum, Record and host output are unchanged, and Rust decode_host stays strict, hence client_only on the unknown-kind fixture.

decisions_for_gate.D1_fallback_shape: Recommended: an unknown entry kind decodes to {kind:unknown, raw_kind:string, text:string|null, seq, at}. The fallback applies only when o.kind is a string that is not one of the six; a missing or non-string kind, or a known kind with bad fields, stays bad_request. seq and at stay required uints. text = o.text if it is a string, else null: the plain text a client renders, say for a future thinking entry. Other fields are dropped, like any unknown field. encodeHostMessage maps it back to {kind:raw_kind, seq, at}, plus text when non-null; that is the decoded_wire of the fixture. types.ts adds the arm | {kind: unknown; raw_kind: string; text: string|null} to the wire TranscriptEntry, not Open<> on kind, which would lose narrowing. unknown becomes a reserved kind the host must never emit. Alternative A: keep the whole entry as raw: Record<string, unknown>, the precedent being unknown_event keeping its payload. That gives an exact round trip and no decoded_wire, at the cost of an untyped bag every renderer has to dig into. Alternative B: no text, just {kind:unknown, raw_kind, seq, at}.
decisions_for_gate.D2_readme_wording: Versioning, README:181-182, becomes: - **Clients ignore unknown fields** and render unknown enum values (agent kind, host, status, PR state, transcript entry kind) as plain text. A transcript entry whose `kind` is a string this build does not know decodes to `{kind: "unknown", raw_kind, text, seq, at}` (`text` is the string `text` of the entry, else `null`; other fields are dropped), so a new entry kind does not bump `v`. `unknown` is reserved and is never a host entry kind. Tolerance, README:242-245: add transcript entry kind to the kept-as-string list; add: and reads an unknown transcript entry kind as the `unknown` fallback rather than failing the event; and end with: An unknown `v` is `unsupported_version` in both directions, checked before `type`, `proto` and every field. The Reopened-if lines stay as they are; this gate approval is the recorded reopening. No other README edits: the v:1.0, null-payload and Babel notes are untouched.
decisions_for_gate.D3_utf8Length: A lone surrogate counts 3 bytes, as TextEncoder and WTF-8 do. Alternative: reject lone surrogates in TS str() as bad_request for exact host parity; a wider change, not recommended now.
decisions_for_gate.D4_proto_key: __proto__ survives via Object.defineProperty, as in the Rust BTreeMap. Alternative: reject it as bad_request in both copies; needs a Rust change, not recommended.

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.

findings.issue: encodeHostMessage applies unknownEntryWire as a JSON.stringify replacer over the WHOLE message, not just transcript entries. Any object anywhere with kind 'unknown' and a string raw_kind gets rewritten. Two raw passthroughs are hit: result.ok and unknown_event.payload. Probe: decode then encode of {v:1,type:'result',id:'a',ok:{kind:'unknown',raw_kind:'x',detail:1}} gives ok:{kind:'x'}, so detail is lost and the kind is changed; an unknown_event payload of the same shape is rewritten the same way. Before this diff both round-tripped exactly. Not a blocker: encodeHostMessage has no production caller today (only the two fixture suites), and a payload has to mimic the reserved fallback. Still, scope the mapping to batch entries (event transcript-appended payload.entries) before any TS host or mock uses the encoder.

The fixture compares only the re-encoded wire, so the decoded D1 shape is never asserted at runtime. tsc catches a missing raw_kind and text:undefined. But a decoder that cast-passed the raw kind through, e.g. {kind: o.kind as any, text, seq, at}, would still pass every gate. One unit test asserting decodeHostMessage(...).payload.entries[1] equals {kind:'unknown', raw_kind:'thinking', text:'hmm', seq:1, at:...} and entries[2].text === null would lock it.

Edge behaviour, checked by probe and consistent with D1 as written. A host kind 'unknown' decodes to {kind:'unknown', raw_kind:'unknown', text, ...} and re-encodes to kind 'unknown': a faithful round trip, and a host breaking the reservation renders as plain text, which is sane. kind '' and kind 'toString' also take the fallback. A host-sent raw_kind field is dropped like any unknown field.
